A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–L. All 36 corresponding page bodies match in text and rendered content; differences are confined to the publication header and arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and CIFAR-100 evaluations, plus few-shot experiments and Tiny ImageNet results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original synthetic, CIFAR-100, few-shot, and Tiny ImageNet experimental results.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same Bayesian teachers obtained through variational inference or Laplace approximation and the same response-based distillation procedure. No algorithm, objective, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic classification data, CIFAR-100 standard and few-shot settings, and Tiny ImageNet evaluations, including Appendices E, G, and J.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: Table 1 retains deterministic, MCMI, TTDA, MSE, and no-KD comparisons, while Table 3 retains KD, DIST, DKD, and WTTM under the same teacher-student comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices E–J retain identical data splits, model pairs, training budgets, optimizers, temperature and distillation-weight configurations, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The synthetic noise and correlation analyses, convergence-stability measurements, few-shot comparisons, temperature sensitivity, and Monte Carlo sample-count analyses are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five-run accuracy summaries and seed information, Appendix K uncertainty entries, and 15-run standard deviations for the synthetic analyses in Appendix E.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and Figures 1–7 contain identical results, with no added or removed entries. For example, both versions report Table 1 student accuracies of 73.63% with the Bayesian teacher and 69.36% with the deterministic teacher for ResNet-50 to WRN-16-2.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B–D retain identical definitions, assumptions, propositions, convergence theorems, and proofs, including the Dirichlet-perturbed probability analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about variance reduction, convergence, and Bayesian teachers. The stated gains of up to 4.27% accuracy and 30% less convergence noise are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning calibration, convergence stability, and stochastic teacher predictions are unchanged. Appendix L retains the same limitations concerning optimization assumptions, noise modeling, and Bayesian computational cost.

D1.justification: The appendices retain identical data-generation instructions, hyperparameters, training schedules, Monte Carlo settings, implementation descriptions, and software links. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list are unchanged, including the distinctions drawn between this work and prior distillation and Bayesian-learning research.

P1.justification: v2 adds the running header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp from v1, 4 January 2026, to v2, 7 July 2026. Body wording and document organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The added publication header and revised first-page margin stamp introduce limited visual changes. Figures, tables, captions, equations, and body layout remain identical throughout the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: The only changes are the publication header and arXiv stamp. The scientific content, experimental evidence, proofs, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
